findings.text: Distributor address map places control at zero, counter at four and identification at eight, group setting at 128, enable set at 256 with clear 128 later, pending set at 512 with clear 128 later, active set at 768 with clear 128 later, priority table at 1024, target table at 2048, configuration table at 3072, software interrupt at 3840, SGI pending clear at 3856 and SGI pending set at 3872.

Distributor enable uses one for on and zero for off, low level trigger encodes as zero, full 32-bit clear mask is all ones, SGI enable covers low sixteen bits while PPI clear covers high sixteen bits, identification splits into twelve bit implementer from zero, four bit revision from twelve, four bit variant from sixteen and eight bit product from twenty four.

Virtualization control block places hypervisor control at zero, type at four, machine control at eight, maintenance status at sixteen, empty interrupt status pair at thirty two and thirty six, empty list status pair at forty eight and fifty two, active priority at two forty and first list register at two fifty six.

Hypervisor control enables function and several maintenance interrupts across bits zero through seven with end count in top five bits, list registers carry ten bit virtual identity low, ten bit physical identity shifted by ten, end bit at nineteen, priority from twenty three, pending and active state at twenty eight and twenty nine with combined state covering both, group one at thirty and hardware flag at thirty one, machine control packs group enables and control flags low with end mode at nine and priority plus binary point fields high, maintenance status signals end and underflow low, virtual priority mask uses five bits from three.
Message interrupt matching uses a single-bit mask derived from PCI MSI bus identity when available else zero, and a single-bit mask derived from platform MSI bus identity.

Virtualization support distinguishes three controller generations in increasing order and describes platform data as generation plus virtual CPU and virtual control resources, mapped CPU interface base, maintenance interrupt number with a flag indicating no masking is needed, plus flags for extended virtual LPIs, revised PEID support and impaired hardware deactivation.
Per CPU accounting keeps a counter with optional snapshot reference, while SMP redirection pairs deferred work with a target CPU number for moving handling.

Each interrupt descriptor combines common and per-chip data, per CPU statistics, a flow handler and action chain, accessor-protected status plus internal state, nested disable and wake depths, total and unhandled counters with aging stamp and broken-line detection, threaded handling counters and oneshot mask with wait queue, reference counting, optional power, proc, debug, sparse, resend, affinity and notification members, SMP pending mask, parent number, owner, name and socket-local alignment.

Domain object links into a global list and holds name, operations, host data, flags, map count, mutex, root and firmware node, bus token, generic chip, device pointers, optional hierarchy parent and MSI parent operations, exit hook and reverse map limits with tree plus sized array, created from an info bundle carrying firmware, flags, sizes, bases, bus, suffix, operations, host, devices, parent, chip info and init or exit hooks.

Domain behavior is customized through match, select, map, unmap and translation callbacks, with hierarchy extensions for allocation, release, activation, deactivation, firmware translation and info query, plus optional debug display.

Descriptor utilities expose per CPU count lookup, conversion from chip data to descriptor, number and chip data retrieval, action presence test, balancing and per CPU classification, sparse lock no-ops and conditional lock class assignment.
Delivery path invokes the descriptor flow handler directly, while locked setters install a handler alone or together with chip and name for the owning descriptor.

Domain helpers locate a wired host with fallback to any bus, instantiate a direct-mapped domain from firmware limits and operations returning null on failure, create mappings with optional affinity, resolve hardware numbers to descriptors, allocate named firmware nodes with optional identifier and parent, and test hierarchy, inter-processor, message-signaled and immutable characteristics via flag checks.

Domain flags mark hierarchy, internally allocated name, per CPU or single inter-processor mode, message signaling variants including isolated, parent and device roles, no-map, destroy-on-remove, immutable MSI, firmware parent matching and reserved implementation space from bit sixteen, bus tokens enumerate wired, MSI families, nexus, inter-processor, wakeup and translation cases, firmware specs carry at most sixteen parameters with a single affinity-valid flag, and firmware node kinds distinguish real, named and named identifier forms.

Descriptor protects fast state with a raw spinlock and serializes request changes with a mutex, domain serializes map changes with its own mutex, and reference counting plus RCU and wait queue coordinate threaded handlers and sparse teardown.

When enabled, hard interrupt entry increments a per CPU nesting count and clears threaded marking on outermost entry with decrement on exit and explicit threaded marking, soft interrupt entry and exit adjust current context count, timer and deferred work entries set a configuration flag for non-hard cases and clear it on exit, while disabled builds reduce all queries and transitions to constants or no-ops.

Fallback builds report no hierarchy or signaling capability, reject firmware info queries and wired message allocation with an error while warning once, ignore wired release with a warning, and make mapping disposal a no-op.
